# HAlert

> Inline feedback for success, information, and problems. Errors announce as alerts; other tones use status.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HAlert` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-alert>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthAlertElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Feedback.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HAlert.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Danger uses role=alert; other tones use role=status. Avoid stacking repeated live announcements for routine updates.
- dismiss only requests dismissal. Remove/hide the component in your handler; it does not own notification storage.

## Public API

title, description: string · tone: Tone · dismissible: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    title?: string;
    description?: string;
    tone?: Tone;
    dismissible?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ tone: "info" }
```

### Events

dismiss()

```ts
type Emits = {
    dismiss: [
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

default

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, title, description

Use `hearth-alert::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HAlert } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';
const visible = ref(true);
</script>

<template>
  <HAlert v-if="visible" title="Preferences saved" description="Your workspace is ready." tone="success" dismissible @dismiss="visible = false" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-alert');
Object.assign(element, {
  "title": "Preferences saved",
  "description": "Your workspace is ready.",
  "tone": "success",
  "dismissible": true
});
element.addEventListener('dismiss', () => element.remove());
mount.append(element);
```
